source.title: Time and Norm Optimal Controls: A Survey of Recent Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Consider the self-adjoint setting discussed in the paper: A is a self-adjoint infinitesimal generator in a separable Hilbert space, H_α = D((μI - A)^α), and a control is called regular when its multiplier z belongs to Z(T) and strongly regular when z belongs to E*. Is it true in this self-adjoint setting that whenever an optimal control reaches a target ȳ satisfying ȳ ∈ D(A), the associated multiplier must actually satisfy z ∈ E*? Equivalently, does regularity imply strong regularity in the borderline case α = 1 of the smoothness relation between the target and the costate?

evidence.quote: Significantly, the proof of Part (a) of Theorem 4.1 excludes the case α = 1, where the implication would be ȳ ∈ D(A) => z ∈ E or, equivalently, regular => strongly regular. Whether this implication holds in the present self adjoint setting seems to be an open problem.

accepted.question_text: Construct a hypersingular time-optimal control in a space where time-optimal controls are unique, for example in a Hilbert space. Here hypersingularity means that the time-optimal control remains strongly singular on every subinterval [α, β] with 0 ≤ α < β ≤ T, rather than merely failing the maximum principle on the whole control interval. The paper gives hypersingular examples only in the very rough space c_0, where uniqueness of time-optimal controls fails, so the open problem is to obtain such an example in a setting with uniqueness.

evidence.quote: It would obviously be better to have an example of an hypersingular control in a space where uniqueness of time optimal controls holds (e.g. a Hilbert space) but we don’t know of any.
